The CFO's 'lumpy' and 'not double-digit, probably' remarks, the capacity that arrives only in late Q2/early Q3 FY27, and SG&A pressure argue the qualitative tone will not lift FY27 above the street.

findings.finding: Q4 new orders will compare against a $934M Q3 record (book-to-bill 3.0x) that included a one-off data-center award of more than $400M. Management said no further near-term projects above $400M are in the pipeline and that book-and-burn averages about $75M a quarter. Q4 orders are therefore likely to fall sequentially by half or more, and book-to-bill may land near 1.0-1.4x on revenue of about $330M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders are the line this name trades on. Q4 FY25: EPS beat by $0.44 and orders flat at $271M, stock -11.3%. Q3 FY26: record orders offset a revenue miss, -13.9% after hours recovered to -3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sequential drop is foreseeable, and sophisticated holders should expect it. But the headline comparison (orders down about 50% q/q) is what the wire prints first, and on Q4 FY25 a weak order headline cost 11% despite a beat. If the market had fully discounted it, the November 2025 reaction would not have happened on a similar setup.
findings.independence: The Q3 release gives the same mega-order composition: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080420/000008042026000103/ex991-powlq3xfy2026earning.htm (same company source, so one finding).

EPS missed in 2 of the last 3 quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 revenue miss: -13.9% after hours, closed -3.8%. The Q1 FY26 EPS beat rose +16.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still sits at +10-15% y/y while the company's own run-rate is +7-9%. If the street had taken the CFO's remark on board, the revenue estimates would cluster near $315-320M rather than $328-342M. Capped small because the revenue bar is disputed across sources and the remark's timeframe is ambiguous in the transcript.

findings.finding: Gross margin faces a tough comparison: Q4 FY25 printed 31.4%, helped by favorable project closeouts. In FY26, 9-month net favorable contract-estimate changes fell to $12.8M from $15.1M, management flagged inflation in copper, aluminum, steel and engineered components plus SG&A pressure from standing up new facilities, and Q3 margin was 30.6%. A y/y margin decline in Q4 is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 margin expansion to 31.4% did not save the stock from -11.3% on orders. Margin is a secondary line here.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $1.52-1.58 against $1.41 a year ago (split-adjusted) implies +8-12%, which needs margin to hold near 30-31% on +10-15% revenue. If the street had built in a closeout-free margin, EPS estimates would sit nearer $1.45.
findings.independence: Q3 call on inflation headwinds and SG&A: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/10/powell-industries-powl-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ ; Q4 FY25 GM 31.4%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80420/000008042025000145/ex991-powlq4xfy2025earning.htm

findings.finding: Texas paused data-center approvals inside Powell's fiscal Q4. Gov. Abbott halted ERCOT grid-connection approvals (reported Aug 10) and TCEQ environmental permits from Sep 21. On Nov 3, governor-elect Hinojosa won on a promised moratorium on all new data-center approvals; Texas is cited as about 30% of US projects. Powell is Houston-based, commercial & other industrial (incl. data center) is 40% of its backlog, and its 10-Q lists data-center legislation as a risk factor. The Q4 order intake and the call's data-center pipeline commentary will be read through this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Powell print with a data-center policy shock. The Nov 4-5 sector sell-off took POWL to its $121 low.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the whole power complex sold off on it Nov 4-5 and POWL with it. What is unpriced is Powell's own exposure, which the company has not quantified. Its $400M+ award spans 'at least five North American facilities' with no location given. This is a proxy, not a company confirmation, and is sized small. Net of the rest: oil & gas, utility (24% of backlog) and petrochemical (30% with O&G) are untouched by it.
findings.independence: Texas Tribune on Hinojosa's pledge: https://texastribune.org/2026/11/04/data-center-texas-pause-gina-hinojosa-governor-policies/ ; Tikr on the Nov 5 sell-off ('forced control on CapEx'): https://www.tikr.com/blog/vertiv-sinks-another-16-as-data-center-selloff-deepens-forced-control-on-capex

findings.finding: Peers and competitors that reported the same Jul-Sep quarter after Powell last spoke all showed accelerating electrical demand. Eaton's electrical data-center orders more than doubled on a rolling 12-month basis, its electrical backlog was about $20.4B (+46%), and it raised FY26 EPS guidance. Vertiv's organic orders more than doubled and it raised guidance (Oct 28). Hubbell's data-center sales rose more than 80% and its utility T&D/substation backlog kept building (Oct 27).
findings.link: Same products and end markets: Eaton is a direct competitor in switchgear and power distribution for data centers and utilities; Hubbell sells utility substation/T&D equipment into the same utility capex that is 24% of Powell's backlog; Vertiv sells data-center power gear into the same hyperscale projects. No shared-customer figure is disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured as a read-through for POWL. Powell's Q3 record orders coincided with strong peer data-center demand.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer prints are public, and POWL fell anyway on the policy scare, so the market has chosen policy over demand evidence. If the peer read had been carried into POWL, its 20-day return would not be -8.5%. Sized small because peer data center demand is not Powell's order book.

findings.finding: First FY27 commentary: the street carries FY27 revenue of $1.48B (+24.5%) and EPS of $6.99 (+30%). Management gives no number, but said on the Q3 call that Powell is 'well positioned to deliver another year of strong financial performance in fiscal 2027'. About $1.3B of backlog converts within 12 months of June 30, plus about $75M a quarter of book-and-burn, which roughly supports the street. Two cautions: new capacity (the Jacintoport yard and a 300k sq ft lease) only produces from late Q2/early Q3 FY27, and the CFO expects lumpy revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Powell does not guide numerically. Its first-year commentary in Nov 2025 ('margin profile sustainable', 'seasonal softness in Q1') coincided with -11.3%, driven by orders.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is unknown; filed so the judges see that the street's FY27 needs a sharp revenue step-up the company has only qualitatively endorsed. If the market believed the $1.48B, the stock would not trade at about 22x FY27 EPS with targets 65% above it.
findings.independence: Street FY27 numbers: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/powl/forecast/ (independent of the transcript).

findings.finding: The balance sheet funds the capacity ramp: cash and short-term investments were $634M at June 30 with no debt, and contract liabilities (customer advances) rose from $297.9M to $466.4M in nine months on the mega awards. This leaves room for the $70-100M greenfield plant and M&A management flagged, with no financing need.

findings.why_not_priced: Known. Filed because a greenfield or M&A decision announced with the print would be funded internally; it is not a dilution or credit risk.

baseline_tension: The evidence is close to balanced, like the skew (+1.96, 'balanced'). The slight negative lean (orders normalising, revenue bar above the company's run-rate, margin comp) goes against a 50%-off-the-high setup with rising short interest, and partly with the 5-day run-up, which has already taken some relief. p_up is held near 50 for that reason.
